chequeos.detalle: two real instances (cifi, cifi-nuevo) running this exact combination in redroid-forge-prod, both pinned to the same 2 physical cores; 4+ days of uptime with no crash or restart before the full jg-dashboard migration started

live scrcpy (real video) plus the built-in preview watched simultaneously on the typical heaviest in-game scene, both instances concurrently: no visible stutter, despite the pair of cores measuring 96-97% busy (mpstat) at the time

switching from software to hardware encode (this combination's hwenc module) measured as freeing ~40% of one core per instance -- the actual bottleneck for this specific game is its own CPU-bound logic (Unity's engine), not the encode

validaciones.notas: Not a dedicated test campaign like the hwenc/gapps entries above -- real production use of the exact combination behind the jg-dashboard -> redroid-forge-prod migration (see project memory, 17/11/2026). The user module `cifi` (the per-instance watchdog) is deliberately left out of `modulos`: user modules are excluded from the known-combinations signature by design (see MODULE-AUTHORING.md's esModuloDeUsuario), not because it was absent on the real instances -- both cifi and cifi-nuevo actually run it.

chequeos.detalle: redroid-forge-prod updated to the hwenc daemon of redroid-hwenc v0.3.0: the shared VA-API daemon stays flat (~55-60 MB) under real encode instead of growing ~27 KB per frame (it used to reach 3-4.5 GB in 12-17 h on this host)

two viewers of the same instance at once (scrcpy plus the built-in expanded viewer): the daemon log on prod shows one encoder slot per stream (distinct stream_id values from the instance's Codec2 process, after the instance was recreated to pick up the new component) -- no black/frozen video from crossed P-frame references
updating the app (1.0.0-beta.2 -> beta.3) with both instances left running: the hwenc daemon and the cifi watchdogs came back on their own at app start, no instance restarted

validaciones.notas: Second validation of the same combination: what changed underneath (hwenc daemon v0.3.0 and its Android component with stream_id) on the same production host and the same two real instances. Module manifest versions are unchanged.
